artifacts.notes: Exact remote facsimile record only; no PDF payload is installed. Existing 1962-Missal research uses the page images as its controlling textual witness, but that research role does not collapse this artifact into the separate Benziger edition or create a publication binding. Why the status stays `unresolved` rather than moving either way. It does not become `licensed`, because adopting the CC tag would mean accepting a stranger's assertion as a grant, and the contradicting upload of the same bytes shows what that assertion is worth. It does not become `public-domain`, because the 1962 typical edition's own status is a separate question this record has never answered and does not answer now: the scan's rights and the book's rights are two things, and a digitization can be free while the book is not, or the reverse. `unresolved` also keeps the guard that matters, since TRACKABLE_RIGHTS excludes it and nothing may install the payload. What the reopening settles is narrower and worth stating: even reading the CC tag at face value, NC and ND govern copying, distribution and adaptation, and this repository does none of the three to the scan. It stores a hash, retains no bytes, publishes no page image, and the English it collates comes from the 1861 Cummiskey rather than from these images. The unanswered question is therefore not the scan's licence at all but the underlying edition's status, which is where TASK-114 should continue.

passages.context: Read at the artifact's embedded text layer. passages.context: The complete bull was read visually at the rendered page images. It narrates the commission to restore the Missal ad pristinam sanctorum Patrum normam ac ritum, imposes the book on the churches named, and expressly exempts churches whose rite was approved from its first institution by the Apostolic See or whose custom of celebrating had been continuously observed for more than two hundred years (a quibus ... nequaquam auferimus), permitting such churches to adopt the new Missal with the consent of the bishop or prelate and the chapter. It grants perpetual leave to use the Missal freely and lawfully absque ullo conscientiae scrupulo, aut aliquarum poenarum, sententiarum et censurarum incursu; decrees nihil unquam addendum, detrahendum, aut immutandum esse under pain of the pope's indignation, addressing patriarchs, administrators and all ecclesiastical dignitaries including cardinals in virtue of holy obedience, and separately threatening printers; and states that priests may not be compelled by anyone to change this Missal, nor may these letters at any time be revoked or modified. The bull legislates nothing about the language of the Mass.
passages.locus: Bulla Quo primum of Pius V, 14 July 1570, front matter, artifact PDF pp. 3-4

passages.context: Read visually at the rendered page image. The decree declaring this Vatican edition typical states that, a new body of rubrics having been approved by John XXIII in the motu proprio Rubricarum instructum and promulgated by the Congregation the following day, it could scarcely fail to happen that the same Congregation should prepare a new edition of the Roman Missal fully accommodated to that code of rubrics. The decree gives the motu proprio's date as 23 July 1960; the Congregation's own general decree promulgating the code, printed later in the same book and dated 26 July 1960, gives 25 July, which alone is consistent with this decree's postero die. The discrepancy is internal to the edition and is not resolved here.
passages.locus: Decretum of the Sacred Congregation of Rites, 23 June 1962, front matter, artifact PDF p. 2
